problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[2,5]\times [0,5]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-25 \\ {x}^{2}-y-20\end{aligned}].
$$

Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts at ${x}_{0}=[5,\,0]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[5,\,5]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).

| ${x}_{2}≈[$ | {{field-1}} | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $2.727$ |  |  |
worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-25) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-25) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-y-20) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-y-20)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x & 2y \\ 2x & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}2x & 2y \\ 2x & -1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-25 \\ {x}^{2}-y-20\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}2x & 2y \\ 2x & -1\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-25 \\ {x}^{2}-y-20\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}2(5) & 2(5) \\ 2(5) & -1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}(5)^{2}+(5)^{2}-25 \\ (5)^{2}-5-20\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}10 & 10 \\ 10 & -1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}25 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{10\cdot (-1)-10\cdot 10}[\begin{aligned}-1 & -10 \\ -10 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}25 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{110}[\begin{aligned}-25 \\ -250\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{105}{22} \\ \frac{30}{11}\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}4.773 \\ 2.727\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
